title.purpose: The title of a line (discovery or open question); width axis set per chapter.

handoff.purpose: The single sentence that closes a chapter.

body.purpose: Reading text in STIX Two Text, max 64ch; 1.0625rem at 600px and below.

label.purpose: Years, wavelength, rail readout, thread links; Archivo width 100, tabular figures, sentence case.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Entrances, hover, press and tick states.

motion.name: ease-in-out

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Scale to 0.97 on buttons, 0.995 on line rows.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Hover fills, tick scaling, title slide, underline thickening, menu open/close.

motion.name: panel-open
motion.purpose: grid-template-rows 0fr to 1fr; content fades in over 320ms after 90ms.

motion.name: title-reveal
motion.purpose: Chapter title words rise out of a clip on entry.

motion.name: band-unroll
motion.purpose: Hero band clip-path reveal on load; lines stand up at 300ms each in sequence.

motion.name: flash
motion.purpose: Highlight sweep across a rule reached by a thread link.

motion.name: reduced
motion.purpose: Reduced motion replaces all transforms, clips and blur with short fades.

narrative.overview:
The system is Fraunhofer's chart of the solar spectrum laid on its side and scrolled from red to past the visible. The ground is the palette: every era is a full-bleed field of one saturated OKLCH colour, and the page moves through eleven of them, oxblood to near-black indigo. Content sits on that field as dark absorption lines: black rules that cross edge to edge, in three weights, each one a thing that can be opened. An opened line broadens into a black band.

Everything is flat and square. There are no cards, no rounded corners, no shadows and no glass; a surface is either a colour field, a rule across it, or a near-black band cut into it. Type carries the spectrum too: Archivo runs wide at the red end and condensed at the blue end, so the width of a heading tells you where you are. STIX Two Text, a face made for scientific publishing, does the reading.

Motion has three verbs, unroll, dock and broaden, on strong ease-out curves with transforms and clip-path. Nothing bounces. Reduced motion replaces every transform with a short opacity fade.

**Key Characteristics:
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed saturated colour fields that change hue by position in the sequence
Edge-to-edge horizontal rules in three weights as the only divider and the only interactive row marker
Near-black bands for opened content and for chrome (rail, menu, close, sources)
One variable sans whose width axis tracks the spectrum; one serif for reading
Square corners, no shadows, no layered surfaces
Ink is always a tint of the ground's own hue, never neutral grey

rules.name: The Ground Is The Palette Rule
rules.body: Colour is applied as a whole field. A spectral colour never appears as a button fill, a tag, a border or a highlight on another ground; the only place two spectral colours touch is a gradient between neighbours.

rules.name: The Tinted Ink Rule
rules.body: No neutral grey, pure black or pure white. Every ink, rule and dark band carries chroma 0.02 to 0.03 at the hue of the ground it belongs to.

rules.name: The Ink Follows Lightness Rule
rules.body: Ink is chosen per ground from the table in `build.mjs`: the five grounds from orange to cyan (lightness 0.72 and up) take dark ink, the rest take light ink. A new ground gets its ink by the same test.

rules.name: The Neighbour Gradient Rule
rules.body: Gradients exist only where the spectrum itself is continuous: between one ground and the next (chapter fades, the hero's fall into oxblood) and across the full spectrum band. They are interpolated in OKLCH. The short end of the sequence stops at hue 272.

rules.name: The Width Axis Rule
rules.body: Archivo's width is set by spectral position: 125, 118, 110, 102, 95, 88, 80, 74, 68, 64, 62 across the eleven grounds. Chapter titles, line titles, handoffs and menu rows inherit their chapter's width. Labels and controls stay at 100 everywhere so they read as instrument, not as content.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase and no positive letter-spacing anywhere. Large Archivo is tightened (-0.02em display, -0.01em title); labels are untracked.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every year and count is set in Archivo with tabular numerals so dates align down a column of lines.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow. A thing that needs to separate from the ground does it with a rule, a near-black band, or a 1px contrasting outline (the rail's current tick and cursor carry a 1px dark outline so they read on every hue).

dos: Do give every new section one ground and let it run full-bleed; derive its ink, rule and panel tones from that ground's hue with the formulas in Colors.
Do separate items with a full-width rule and use its thickness (2, 5 or 11px) to say how much the item matters.
Do set Archivo's width from spectral position for headings and at 100 for labels and controls.
Do keep text inside the 78rem wrap, hung from the left edge, with body at 64ch or less.
Do put opened or secondary content in a near-black band tinted to the local hue.
Do interpolate every gradient in OKLCH and only between neighbouring grounds.
Do use ease-out transforms and clip-path for motion, and provide an opacity-only version for reduced motion.
Do keep every interactive target at 44px or more, padding thin lines invisibly.
Do keep plates greyscale and uncaptioned, with credit and licence in Sources.
donts: Don't build cards, tiles or any boxed container; the brief rules out repeated rounded rectangles and gradient-and-glass cards.
Don't round a corner. Radius is 0.
Don't add shadows, glows or backdrop blur.
Don't use a spectral colour as an accent on a different ground.
Don't use neutral grey, `#000` or `#fff`; tint every tone to its hue.
Don't set uppercase or letter-spaced labels.
Don't lay entries out as dated cards beside a centre line; the product rejects the static timeline.
Don't bounce, overshoot or spring any motion.
Don't add a second button style or a filled-at-rest button.
